title: Data Race in Concurrency and Actor Reentrancy
platform_conditions: Swift runtime concurrency semantics (actors, Sendable, structured concurrency); applies wherever Swift runs, including iOS/macOS and server-side Swift
security_mechanism: An actor suspends at every await and is free to run other messages before the suspended one resumes, so a check performed before an await no longer describes the state when the awaited work returns — the balance check passes twice for two concurrent messages, and both deduct. Marking a type @unchecked Sendable or a property nonisolated(unsafe) silences the compiler's data-race analysis without adding synchronization, turning shared mutable state into a classic unsynchronized race across queues or Tasks. Weaker atomic-ordering mistakes (relaxed ordering where acquire/release was required in the underlying C/ObjC primitives) and lock poisoning/deadlock in mixed GCD/async code complete the same class.

source_sink_clues.source: Concurrent requests or UI events reaching the same actor/queue; attacker-controlled values that drive two interleaved check-then-act sequences (double-spend, double-redeem, TOCTOU on permission flags).
source_sink_clues.sink: State checks separated from the mutation by an await inside an actor; @unchecked Sendable conformance on stateful types; nonisolated(unsafe) on mutable properties; shared vars mutated from multiple Tasks/DispatchQueues without a lock

tracking_guards: Check the security-relevant condition is re-validated after every await (or the read-check-write sequence is a single non-suspending critical section); check @unchecked Sendable types actually serialize access with a lock or confinement; check permission/authorization flags are not cached in mutable shared state that another request can flip.
not_candidate_when: The actor method performs its check and mutation without any intervening await, the shared state is immutable or actor-isolated with no @unchecked escape, or the operation is idempotent so an interleaved second execution cannot change the security outcome.
synthetic_vulnerable_example: if balance >= amount { await deduct(); balance -= amount }
public_references: CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/362.html
